headline: Bull's plan only works if you buy $11 below the current price; buying now, the first prize is about half the risk, and Ether is still under every important line.

messages.text: Fair correction first: I said buyers were outnumbered 0.69 to 1. A fresh check shows 1.19, so that point flipped and I'm dropping it. That order list is tiny and changes every minute anyway.

messages.reply_to: Bull: RSI is 26... sellers are very tired
messages.text: RSI (a speed meter, under 30 = fell very fast) is 27.1 on the hourly chart. 'Fell fast' does not mean 'done falling'. The hourly down-push meter (MACD) is still getting stronger, not weaker.

messages.reply_to: Bull: Big volume at the bottom often means panic selling
messages.text: Hourly trading is 7 times normal, but no higher low has formed yet. The latest 5-minute candles trade at only 0.4 times normal. A bounce on thin trading is easy to knock down.

messages.reply_to: Bull: There is a floor nearby. The lowest price today was $2,028
messages.text: A floor only counts if it holds. $2,028 is just 2% below, and the same news site Bull quotes is asking whether $2,000 is at risk. Today's low is where the flush ended, not proof buyers will defend it.

messages.reply_to: Bull: My plan risks little: buy near $2,060
messages.text: Ether is $2,071 right now, not $2,060. From $2,071 the stop at $2,022 risks about $49. The first target at $2,096 wins about $25, so you win about 50 cents for every $1 you risk.

messages.reply_to: Bull: Bets that the price rises cost almost nothing extra
messages.text: Fear score 32 means 'scared', not 'panic bottom'. And big US Ethereum funds lost about $272M from Nov 2 to 5 (I opened the report and added it up: -140, -85, +53, -100 in millions), after a record 23 days of outflows. Big money is still not buying.

argument:
Update on my own Round 1 claims. The order-book ratio has flipped from 0.69 to 1.19 on a fresh pull (bids $1.63M vs asks $1.37M); I withdraw it as evidence, and note the top-100 book holds only ~$3M so it is noise. I could not confirm the ETH-vs-BTC headline beyond its title, so I drop it. The ETF outflow figure is now verified: Mitrade citing Farside lists Nov 2 -$139.7M, Nov 3 -$85.3M, Nov 4 +$53M, Nov 5 -$99.9M, net -$271.9M (my sum), plus Glassnode's 23-day record outflow streak through Oct 30.

Fresh data (13:58 UTC): price 2071.25. 1h RSI 27.1, 15m RSI 30.6, 5m RSI 36.8. Bull is right that short-term momentum is ticking up off the low, but all three timeframes still have EMA9 below EMA21 and price below SMA50 and SMA200. The 1h MACD histogram is -2.73 against -1.22 before, so downside momentum is still expanding. 1h volume is 7.07x average while 5m volume is 0.4x: the capitulation bar already printed, and the current bounce is unsupported.

Plan math. Bull's 1:1.4 and 1:2.2 assume a fill at 2060, which is 11 below market and may never fill if price lifts. A market entry at ~2071 with Bull's 2022 stop risks 49. Targets pay 25 (VWAP 2096.14, 0.5:1), 42 (2113, 0.86:1) and 71 (2142, 1.45:1). Only the farthest target beats 1:1, and it sits beyond the 1h SMA20 (2116.8) and EMA21 (2113.7) resistance cluster that must be cleared first. The stop is about 2.3x the 1h ATR of 21, so it is not too tight, but that just means more dollars at risk.

Funding is +0.0025%, so longs still pay shorts; leverage was not fully washed out despite a $432M liquidation headline (headline only).

evidence.claim: 1h RSI 27.1, 15m 30.6, 5m 36.8; 1h MACD hist -2.73 (prev -1.22); all timeframes below SMA50/SMA200; 1h vol 7.07x, 5m vol 0.4x
evidence.plain: Still under every important line, down-pressure still growing on the hourly chart, and the current bounce has little trading behind it.
Price is $11 above Bull's entry. The first prize is about $25 up; the stop Bull picked is about $49 down.
evidence.source: Binance public API via tools/market_data.py; arithmetic by Bear

evidence.claim: US spot ETH ETFs net -$271.9M Nov 2-5 (-139.7, -85.3, +53, -99.9); 23 straight outflow days through Oct 30
evidence.plain: Big investors keep pulling money out of Ethereum funds. I opened the article and added up the days myself.
evidence.source: Mitrade citing Farside Investors; streak per Glassnode

evidence.claim: Order book top-100 bid/ask ratio now 1.19 (was 0.69)
evidence.plain: I'm admitting this flipped. It is only about $3M of orders in total, so it is a weak signal either way.

evidence.claim: AMBCrypto: Will ETH's $432M liquidation shock put $2K support at risk?
evidence.plain: Even the article Bull uses for 'floor' asks whether $2,000 breaks (headline only, article not opened).

evidence.claim: Fear and Greed 32 (Fear), previous 29; perp funding +0.0025%
evidence.plain: People are scared but not at an extreme, and longs still pay a small fee, so the washout may not be finished.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: RSI 26.6 means sellers are tired, bounce due
rebuttals.response: RSI 27.1 (1h) only says the drop was fast. In a trend it can stay oversold. 1h MACD histogram went from -1.22 to -2.73, so downside momentum is expanding. 15m and 5m RSI have ticked up (30.6, 36.8) but price is still below all averages.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: 6.93x volume = capitulation, panic runs out of steam
rebuttals.response: A volume spike is not a bottom by itself; no higher low has formed. 5m volume has dried up to 0.4x, so the bounce is unconfirmed.
Only 2% below price, and the cited article asks if $2K is at risk (headline only). Bull's own stop at 2,022 sits barely under the low, so a normal flush through it ends the trade.
Valid only from a 2,060 fill. At market (2,071) risk is 49: reward is 0.5x to VWAP, 0.86x to 2,113, and 1.45x only at 2,142, past a resistance cluster at 2,113-2,117.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bull: Fear 32 and low funding leave room for a bounce
rebuttals.response: 32 is mild fear, not an extreme. Funding is still positive, meaning longs are still paying. Neither is a capitulation signal.

plan_flaws: Entry 2,055-2,070 is below market 2,071; a limit at 2,060 may not fill, and at market the R:R to VWAP is ~0.5:1.
Risk from 2,071 to the 2,022 stop is ~49; targets pay 25 / 42 / 71 (0.5 / 0.86 / 1.45).
Targets 2,113 and 2,142 sit behind the 1h EMA21 (2,113.7) and SMA20 (2,116.8) resistance cluster.
Stop 2,022 is only ~6 under the 24h low 2,028.32; a normal liquidation wick could take it out.
plan_flaws_plain: Bull wants to buy $11 below where Ether is now, and it may never get there.
Buying now, you risk about $49 to win about $25 at the first target.
Two of Bull's three targets sit right under a crowded ceiling where sellers have been showing up.
The safety exit is only $6 below today's low, so one more shake-out could stop you out.
conditions_to_reconsider: An hourly close back above about $2,117 on higher than usual trading, a higher low above $2,028, and a few days of US Ethereum funds no longer losing money.
